given: One SKU holds stock at two different locations (two records sharing the SKU)
when: The team member opens the home stock table
then: Both (sku, location) records appear as two separate rows, not collapsed into a single per-SKU row
architectural_notes: E2E: defends the per-(sku, location) addressing established by PI1 (composite UNIQUE(sku, location)) all the way to the browse view. The repository (app/repositories/) returns one row per (sku, location) with no per-SKU grouping, the service (app/services/) preserves that grain, and the SPA renders each as a distinct row. Owner module: stock-repository list query + stock-service. Verified against real branch rows seeding one SKU at two locations; the read path must not collapse or de-duplicate on SKU alone.

rationale: Asserts that stock is addressed per (sku, location) in the browse view (one SKU at two locations yields two rows), distinct from AC1 which uses different SKUs; a build could pass AC1 yet collapse same-SKU rows and lose a location.
